closing.summary: Best bits are fibre, a low glycemic index, strong plant protein, and excellent minerals. Weak spots are thin vitamin support, possible digestive discomfort, and dry-bean preparation. Best for steady energy, digestion, and budget meals because fibre supports bowel health, while protein and starch make them a substantial staple. Pair them with vitamin C-rich vegetables to improve iron absorption.

scenes.narrationText: 2.2 grams of fat. Saturated fat is only 0.22 grams, an excellent low mark. Polyunsaturated fat is just 0.36 grams, so the beans do not provide much useful fat either. That is not a major problem though. Legumes are supposed to win through slow carbs, fibre, and protein, not fat.

scenes.narrationText: Vitamins barely show up here. Vitamin E is only 1% daily value and vitamin C is 0%. Vitamin C helps the body absorb plant-based iron, so pairing cannellini beans with peppers, lemon, or other vitamin C-rich foods makes nutritional sense. On their own though, the vitamin section is a clear weakness.

Zinc is the softer mark at 25% daily value, but that is still useful for immune function and tissue repair. For legumes, this is a genuinely strong mineral section.

scenes.narrationText: The cons next: can be rough on digestion. Their fermentable carbohydrates feed gut bacteria, but can also produce gas and bloating. Dry beans take time and planning. Soaking and a full cook make them less convenient than opening a can. They must be cooked properly. Cannellini are white kidney beans, and raw or undercooked beans can retain a natural lectin called P H A. Proper cooking brings it down to safe levels.
